ownership_decision.invariant: A trial run is dispatched with a stand-in for exactly the unretired mcp_tools rows its Skill Version declares in allowed-tools, each without the server address.

boundary_decision.interaction: ingest-run-mcp-stand-ins: the run context reads the offered tools through its registry fact adapter at the composition root; it never imports ingest

domain_forces: A Skill that declares a listed MCP tool must be triable without any MCP server or credential.
The list changes after a version is admitted, and a Skill Version never changes.
A name the version declares but the list does not offer must not become a tool the agent can call.
An unreadable list must not read as a version with no tools.
implementation_design.decision: At dispatch, intersect the version manifest allowed-tools with the unretired mcp_tools rows and send reference, purpose and parameters as RunRequest.mcp_tools; the registry fact adapter adds them to the version facts so execution.Service keeps its field budget. A version declaring no mcp__ name never reads the list; an unreadable list fails the dispatch attempt.
invariants_preserved: Skill Version immutability: nothing about the list is stored with the version.
A withheld Skill carries no stand-ins.
The server address never leaves the platform for a trial.
rejected_alternatives: Storing the offered tools with the version at admission: the list changes and the version cannot.
Sending the whole list and letting the runtime intersect: it would hand the sandbox tools the Skill never declared.
A new field on execution.Service for a catalog port: the Service is at its field budget.
implementation_design.counterfactual_check: Dropping mcp_tools from the dispatched request turns the rule test red; the evidence bundle records the run.

contract_change.change: The version facts the run context reads now also carry the offered MCP stand-ins; existing fields are unchanged.

record.statement: A Skill may declare in allowed-tools only MCP tools that operators list in mcp_tools, referenced as mcp__<server>__<tool>; an mcp__ name that no unretired mcp_tools row provides is unlisted, and a name without the mcp__ prefix is never judged against the list.
examples: mcp__calendar__create_event is accepted while mcp_tools lists calendar and create_event, and mcp__calendar__create_events is unlisted.
Read and Bash(git:*) are not MCP names and are never unlisted.

record.statement: An operator adds a row to mcp_tools with a server, tool, purpose, parameters, an HTTPS server_url and a reason, written in one transaction with its audit event; at most one unretired row exists per server and tool, and a second is refused as a conflict.
examples: Adding calendar/create_event twice without retiring the first answers 409 the second time.
A draft with an http address or an uppercase server name is refused before anything is listed.

record.delivery: composition-root fact reader: at dispatch the run context reads, through its registry fact adapter, the unretired mcp_tools rows its Skill Version declares in allowed-tools, and hands their reference, purpose and parameters to the provider as stand-ins

record.statement: A trial run is dispatched with a stand-in for each MCP tool its Skill Version declares in allowed-tools that is on the mcp_tools list and not retired, and for no other mcp__ name; each stand-in carries the tool reference, purpose and parameters and never the server address, so the runtime can answer the call without reaching the tool.
examples: A version declaring Read, a listed mcp__calendar__create_event, a retired mcp__calendar__delete_event and an unlisted mcp__calendar__send_mail is dispatched with one stand-in, mcp__calendar__create_event.
A version declaring only Read and Bash is dispatched with no stand-ins.

approvals.scope: Trial dispatch carries a stand-in for each declared, unretired mcp_tools row (ingest-run-mcp-stand-ins, the run rule); re-cites of the two ingest rules and registry-run-facts-v1 after the code moved
